result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both slides show the correct figures for all three customers and invent no data. B does more with the trade-offs: it colours Fennmark's increase differently, says the revenue effect of this small sample is unknown, and makes a Fennmark rollout plan part of the decision. A covers the trade-off only in small body text, and its headline wraps onto two lines. B leaves a large empty gap in the middle but stays readable. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both slides show correct before/after figures for all three customers and add up the totals correctly ($560 → $435), with no invented data. A colour-codes Fennmark's increase in orange and attaches a rollout-plan condition to the ask, so the 7.5× jump reads as part of the decision. B has a larger decision box, but its headline runs onto two lines and its small paragraph text makes the tradeoff harder to read at a glance.
